meta.version_notes: v1.2 — Added consult_type detection (initial vs follow_up) inferred from the transcript, and made initiation-only items NA for follow-up consults: bmi_weight_target, prior_wl_attempts, dose_escalation, mechanism_of_action, lab_baseline. v1.1 — Replaced 4-tier criticality (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) + holistic /10 domain scores with 3-tier within-domain weights (10/6/2) + binary YES/NO/NA per item. Added deterministic per-item YES rules. Compressed grading bands. Math is now fully deterministic given the per-item statuses.
meta.scope: GLP-1 e-consultations. Applies to both initial prescribing and follow-up titration consults. consult_type (initial|follow_up) is inferred from the transcript per scoring.consult_type_detection and changes ONLY the na_rule of the initiation-only items listed in version_notes; all other items and the math are unchanged.
meta.assessment_methodology: Audio structural analysis (turn count, turn duration, speech activity ratio) combined with GLP-1 clinical quality benchmarks. Audio structural patterns are reliable proxies for consultation quality but do not change the scored composite — they are reported as flags only.

rubric_authority.directive: This rubric is sacrosanct and applies to ALL cases without exception. The LLM scorer, human reviewers, and any downstream automation MUST score every consult strictly against the domains, cross-domain weights, within-domain tier weights (10/6/2), per-item YES rules, composite formula, and grading bands defined in this JSON. No domain may be added, removed, re-weighted, renamed, or re-tagged at scoring time. No item may be inferred, substituted, or skipped because it 'feels less relevant' for a given consult. Per-item statuses are strictly YES, NO, or NA — there is no PARTIAL. If a checklist item is genuinely not applicable (e.g., pregnancy/contraception for a male patient), mark it NA per the YES rule and exclude it from both numerator and denominator. Any change to this rubric must be a versioned update to this file, signed off by the rubric owner.

math.domain_pct_formula: domain_pct = (sum of tier_weight over items with status=YES) / (sum of tier_weight over items with status in {YES, NO}) * 100
math.composite_formula: composite_pct = sum over domains of (domain_pct * cross_domain_weight_pct) / 100
math.rounding: Round both domain_pct and composite_pct to 1 decimal place.
math.n_a_handling: Items with status NA are excluded from BOTH numerator and denominator of the domain_pct.

structural_indicators.purpose: Reported alongside the score as quality signals. They inform interpretation but do NOT change the /100 composite.

metrics.label: Consult duration (minutes)
metrics.note: Borderline–short for a comprehensive GLP-1 initial prescription consult.

metrics.label: Average turn length (seconds)
metrics.interpretation: Higher = more lecture-style; lower = more interactive.

metrics.label: Speech activity (%)
metrics.note: >92% = no pause/reflection time; <70% = audio quality issue.

metrics.label: Diarized talk-time ratio (S0 vs others)
metrics.standard: Interpret alongside qualitative review only — Deepgram S0 is not verified as clinician.
metrics.computation: Requires diarize + utterances: ratio of speaker 0 duration vs all other speakers; value duplicated under legacy key doctor_to_patient_ratio.

consult_type_detection.purpose: Some na_rules depend on whether this is an INITIAL (first prescribing) consult or a FOLLOW_UP consult. Determine consult_type FIRST from the transcript, then apply each item's na_rule. Only the items whose na_rule explicitly references consult_type are affected; every other item is scored identically regardless of consult_type.
consult_type_detection.follow_up_rule: Classify the consult as follow_up ONLY IF the transcript contains a doctor question probing whether the patient is already on a GLP-1, is looking to increase / titrate up their existing dose, or is doing a follow-on / continuation consult (e.g. 'Are you already on a GLP-1?', 'Are you looking to increase your dosage?', 'Is this a follow-up / continuation?') AND the patient affirmatively confirms it (answers yes, or states they are already on / continuing a GLP-1). If there is no such confirmed doctor-question-plus-patient-yes exchange, the consult is initial. When ambiguous, default to initial (this keeps the initiation-only items scored rather than silently excused).

examples.follow_up: Doctor: 'Are you already on a GLP-1, and are you looking to increase the dose?' Patient: 'Yes, I'm on Wegovy 0.5 mg and want to go up to 1 mg.'
examples.initial: No exchange establishing that the patient is already on / continuing a GLP-1; the doctor is starting/prescribing therapy.

checklist.item: MTC/MEN2 family history (absolute contraindication)
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor explicitly asks about thyroid cancer family history OR multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN2) family history at any point in the consult AND the patient's response is captured in the transcript.
checklist.no_rule: NO if the question is not asked, OR is asked too vaguely (e.g., 'any family disease?' without naming thyroid cancer or MEN2), OR the patient never responds.

examples.yes: “Is there any family history of thyroid cancer or pancreatic cancer?”
examples.no: “Any family history of disease?” (too vague — doesn't name thyroid cancer or MEN2).

checklist.item: History of pancreatitis (acute or chronic)
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor explicitly asks about the patient's personal history of pancreatitis (acute or chronic) AND the patient's response is captured. Match the concept by synonym, not exact keyword — 'pancreatitis', 'pancreatic problem', 'pancreas issue', 'pancreatic disease', 'inflammation of the pancreas', etc. all count.
checklist.no_rule: NO if not asked, OR asked too vaguely (e.g., 'any GI issues?' / 'any stomach problems?' without naming the pancreas).

examples.yes: “Is there any history of pancreatitis sir, inflammation of pancreatitis?” OR “Any pancreatic problem / pancreas issue in the past?”

checklist.item: Current medications — insulin/SU (hypoglycemia risk)
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor performs a substantive medication review that specifically captures whether the patient is on insulin OR a sulfonylurea OR another diabetic agent (metformin alone is NOT sufficient because it's not a hypoglycemia-risk drug; the question must be about hypoglycemia-risk meds). If the patient is on insulin or SU, the doctor must also raise hypoglycemia risk for YES.
checklist.no_rule: NO if there is no medication review at all, OR the review is shallow (e.g., 'any weight loss medicine?' only), OR the patient is on insulin/SU and the doctor does not flag hypoglycemia risk.
checklist.na_rule: NA iff the patient is documented as non-diabetic or pre-diabetic AND is not on insulin or a sulfonylurea (no hypoglycemia-risk agent), so hypoglycemia review is not applicable. The diabetic status and medication inference must be supported by transcript content.

examples.yes: Doctor asks “Any insulin or sulfonylurea?” OR confirms full med list including diabetic agents.
examples.no: Doctor only asks “any weight loss medicine?”
examples.na: Patient states they are non-diabetic (or pre-diabetic) and not on any insulin or sulfonylurea.

checklist.item: Pregnancy / contraception status (women)
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff (for a female patient of reproductive age, ~15–50 inclusive) the doctor asks about pregnancy status, contraception use, OR breastfeeding (any one of the three suffices).
checklist.no_rule: NO if the patient is a reproductive-age female and none of pregnancy/contraception/breastfeeding is asked.
checklist.na_rule: NA iff the patient is male, OR is documented as post-menopausal (>55), OR is pre-pubertal. The age inference must be supported by transcript content (patient self-reports age or sex).

examples.yes: “Are you breastfeeding?” OR “Are you on contraception?”

checklist.item: Personal history of gallstones (cholelithiasis risk)
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor explicitly asks about gallstones, cholelithiasis, kidney/gall stones, OR a focused biliary symptom history. Match by synonym, not exact keyword — 'gallstones', 'gallbladder problem', 'gallbladder disease', 'cholelithiasis', 'stones in the gallbladder', etc. all count.
checklist.no_rule: NO if not asked, OR asked too vaguely (e.g., 'any GI issues?' alone).
checklist.na_rule: NA iff the patient self-reports prior cholecystectomy with no other biliary issues (rare; document the reason).

examples.yes: “No kidney stones or gallstones?” OR “Any gallbladder problem / gallbladder disease?”

checklist.item: BMI, current weight, target weight goal
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff (a) the patient's current weight AND height are captured (BMI computable), AND (b) a target weight, weight-loss percentage goal, OR specific weight-loss number is discussed by either party AND acknowledged by the doctor.
checklist.no_rule: NO if weight or height is missing, OR there is no target/goal discussion at all.
checklist.na_rule: NA iff consult_type is follow_up AND the weight target/goal was clearly established previously (i.e., this is a continuation where the goal is treated as already agreed, not re-opened). See scoring.consult_type_detection. For initial consults, never NA.

examples.yes: Weight 112 kg + height 5’9” + patient says “I want to lose 10 kg” and doctor acknowledges.
examples.no: Weight + height captured but no target weight or goal mentioned.
examples.na: Follow-up consult where the weight goal was set at an earlier visit and is treated as already agreed.

checklist.item: Comorbidities: T2DM, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CVD
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff at least 2 of the 4 categories (T2DM, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CVD/heart disease) are addressed in the consult — either through doctor questioning OR patient volunteering, AND the doctor acknowledges the responses.
checklist.no_rule: NO if fewer than 2 categories are addressed.

examples.yes: Patient mentions pre-diabetes and hypertension; doctor acknowledges both.
examples.no: Only diabetes mentioned with no probe of HTN/lipids/CVD.

checklist.item: CKD/renal function (dose adjustment needed)
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor explicitly asks about kidney disease, renal function, eGFR, or creatinine, OR the patient volunteers renal-function info AND the doctor acknowledges or factors it into the dosing decision.
checklist.no_rule: NO if not asked, not volunteered, or volunteered but not acknowledged.

examples.yes: “Any kidney problems? Recent eGFR?”

checklist.item: Previous weight loss attempts and outcomes
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor explicitly asks about previous diet, exercise, medication, or surgical attempts at weight loss, AND the patient describes outcomes (success, duration, regain). Currently being on a GLP-1 from a prior prescription does not count as a 'prior attempt' — it is the current treatment context.
checklist.no_rule: NO if not asked, OR asked but the patient gives no substantive response.
checklist.na_rule: NA iff consult_type is follow_up. This history is expected only at initiation; on a follow-up/continuation consult it is not applicable. See scoring.consult_type_detection.

examples.yes: Patient narrates 80–85 kg pre-corporate, 128 kg post-COVID, then Wegovy 0.25→0.5→1 mg history.
examples.no: “Any diet attempts?” not asked at all.
examples.na: Follow-up consult (patient already on / continuing a GLP-1).

checklist.item: Thyroid disease or nodules history
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor explicitly asks about the patient's OWN thyroid status, nodules, hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, or TSH AND the patient's response is captured. (Family thyroid cancer history is a different item — see Safety: MTC/MEN2.)
checklist.no_rule: NO if not asked, OR only family thyroid history is probed.

examples.yes: “Any thyroid issues yourself?” — patient: “No.”
examples.no: Only family thyroid history is asked.

checklist.item: Eating patterns: emotional eating, binge eating disorder
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor probes eating BEHAVIOR specifically — e.g., emotional eating, binge eating, restrictive patterns, eating frequency, hunger cues, food relationship. A generic diet-content question (“what do you eat?”, “veg or non-veg?”) does NOT count.
checklist.no_rule: NO if only diet content is asked, OR no eating-behavior question.
checklist.na_rule: NA unless an eating disorder, poor response, or behavioural concerns are suspected. Applicable (not NA) iff the transcript surfaces suspicion of an eating disorder, a poor treatment response, or behavioural concerns that warrant probing eating behaviour; otherwise NA. The suspicion must be supported by transcript content.

examples.yes: “Do you eat when stressed?” OR “Any binge episodes?”
examples.no: “What’s your usual diet — junk food or healthy?” (content, not behavior).
examples.na: No indication of an eating disorder, poor response, or behavioural concern in the transcript.

checklist.item: Mental health status (depression, anxiety, eating disorders)
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor asks about depression, anxiety, mood, eating disorder, or general mental health status AND the patient's response is captured.
checklist.no_rule: NO if not asked.
checklist.na_rule: NA unless clinically relevant. Applicable (not NA) iff the transcript surfaces a clinically relevant trigger — psychiatric history, an eating disorder, or an indication for behavioural intervention; otherwise NA. The clinical relevance must be supported by transcript content.

examples.yes: “How are you feeling mood-wise?” OR “Any depression or anxiety?”
examples.no: Not asked despite patient mentioning anxiety symptoms.
examples.na: No psychiatric history, eating disorder, or behavioural-intervention indication in the transcript.

checklist.item: Physical activity level and willingness
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor asks about the patient's CURRENT activity level (frequency or type) AND/OR provides a specific activity prescription tied to the patient's context (e.g., minutes per day, type of exercise).
checklist.no_rule: NO if only generic 'exercise' is mentioned without a context or prescription.

examples.yes: “What exercise do you currently do?” — patient: “Running 4–5 days a week.” OR doctor: “Do brisk walking 40 minutes daily.”

checklist.item: Alcohol intake (addictive transfer risk with GLP-1)
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor explicitly asks about alcohol consumption frequency or quantity.
checklist.no_rule: NO if not asked.

examples.yes: “Do you drink alcohol? How often?”

checklist.item: Sleep quality / obstructive sleep apnea
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor asks about sleep quality, sleep apnea, snoring, or daytime fatigue.
checklist.no_rule: NO if not asked.

examples.yes: “How’s your sleep — any snoring or daytime fatigue?”

checklist.item: Dose escalation schedule (weekly up-titration)
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor explicitly states a multi-step up-titration schedule (e.g., 0.25 mg → 0.5 mg → 1 mg over weeks, OR 2.5 → 5 → 7.5 mg) OR explicitly confirms the patient already understands such a schedule. The schedule must include at least 2 distinct dose steps.
checklist.no_rule: NO if only injection frequency is mentioned (e.g., 'weekly') without a multi-step dose ladder.
checklist.na_rule: NA iff consult_type is follow_up. The full up-titration schedule is expected at initiation; on a follow-up/continuation consult it is not applicable. See scoring.consult_type_detection.

examples.yes: “First 4 weeks 2.5 mg, then 4 weeks 5 mg, then 7.5 mg.”
examples.na: Follow-up consult (patient already on / continuing a GLP-1).

checklist.item: Common side effects: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor names at least 3 of: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, headache, decreased appetite, acidity, indigestion, abdominal pain.
checklist.no_rule: NO if fewer than 3 are named, OR none.

examples.yes: “Acidity, constipation, and diarrhea — normal in 1–2 weeks.” (3 named)

checklist.item: Serious adverse events: pancreatitis, thyroid, gallstones
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor mentions at least 2 of: pancreatitis, thyroid C-cell tumour / MTC risk, gallstones / cholelithiasis, severe hypoglycemia, severe allergic reaction.
checklist.no_rule: NO if fewer than 2 are named, OR if the doctor frames the drug as 'completely safe' / 'no major side effects' (active downplay = NO regardless of counts).

examples.yes: “Pancreatitis is a long-term risk; thyroid C-cell tumour is a black-box warning.”

checklist.item: Mechanism of action explained (GLP-1 receptor agonism)
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor explains how GLP-1 works at a substantive level — receptor agonism, satiety / appetite suppression, gastric emptying, OR insulin / glucose response.
checklist.no_rule: NO if mechanism is not explained, OR explained too vaguely (e.g., ‘it helps with sugar’ alone).
checklist.na_rule: NA iff consult_type is follow_up. The mechanism explanation is mandatory at initiation but not expected on a follow-up/continuation consult. See scoring.consult_type_detection.

examples.yes: “GLP-1 mimics a gut hormone that increases satiety and slows gastric emptying.”
examples.no: “It will help your blood sugar and weight.” (too vague).
examples.na: Follow-up consult (patient already on / continuing a GLP-1).

checklist.item: Protein target (≥1.2g/kg/day to preserve muscle mass)
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor counsels the patient to increase/prioritise protein intake to preserve muscle mass — either as a specific numeric target (grams per day OR grams per kg of body weight per day) OR as general protein counselling by synonym (e.g. 'high-protein diet', 'protein-rich meals', 'increase protein intake', 'eat more protein'). A numeric gram/kg target is NOT required.
checklist.no_rule: NO if protein intake is not addressed at all.

examples.yes: “70 grams of protein per day, half from powder, half from diet.” OR “Focus on a high-protein diet / protein-rich meals / increase your protein intake.”
examples.no: Protein intake not mentioned at all.

checklist.item: Long-term diet strategy beyond drug cessation
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor explicitly discusses what happens to diet after the GLP-1 is stopped, sustainability, weight-maintenance phase strategy, OR regain prevention.
checklist.no_rule: NO if there is no discussion of post-cessation diet or long-term maintenance.

examples.yes: “When you stop the medicine, weight regain is common unless you have built habits like X, Y, Z.”

checklist.item: Foods to avoid / slow gastric emptying advice
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor names specific food types or foods to avoid, OR gives slow-gastric-emptying-related dietary guidance (e.g., small frequent meals, avoiding heavy fatty foods).
checklist.no_rule: NO if no specific foods or guidance.

examples.yes: “Avoid large fatty meals; eat small portions to manage nausea.”

checklist.item: Hydration guidance (dehydration common with nausea)
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor mentions hydration, fluid intake, or dehydration risk. Match by synonym, not exact keyword — 'drink more water', 'stay hydrated', 'increase fluids', 'keep yourself hydrated', 'drink plenty of fluids', etc. all count.
checklist.no_rule: NO if not mentioned.

examples.yes: “Drink at least 2 litres of water daily — dehydration is common with nausea.” OR “Stay hydrated / drink more water / increase your fluids.”

checklist.item: Lab baseline: HbA1c, lipids, LFT, amylase/lipase
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor orders or explicitly references at least 2 of: HbA1c, lipid panel, LFT, amylase/lipase, KFT/RFT, TSH — either as pre-treatment baseline or as a monitoring panel.
checklist.no_rule: NO if fewer than 2 named, OR only one ('pancreatic profile' alone counts as 1).
checklist.na_rule: NA iff consult_type is follow_up AND no new labs are clinically indicated (a routine titration follow-up). Baseline labs are applicable at initiation OR whenever clinically indicated — so if the transcript shows a clinical trigger for labs on the follow-up (new symptoms, abnormal prior results, a dose change requiring monitoring), the item remains applicable and is NOT NA. See scoring.consult_type_detection.

examples.yes: “Before starting, do HbA1c, lipid panel, LFT, KFT.”
examples.no: “Get a pancreatic profile in 3 months.” (1 lab).
examples.na: Routine follow-up consult with no new clinical indication for labs.

checklist.item: Follow-up schedule: 4 weeks, 3 months, 6 months
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor arranges a future touchpoint with a specific timeframe (in weeks or months). The follow-up intent may be phrased in any equivalent way — 'follow-up', 'review', 'reconnect', 'update me', 'next visit', 'check in', 'see you', 'come back', 'monitoring', etc. — so long as a specific timeframe is attached.
checklist.no_rule: NO if no specific timeframe is given (vague ‘follow up later’ / ‘come back if needed’ does NOT count).

examples.yes: “Follow up after 1 month” OR “let’s review in 3 months” OR “reconnect in 4 weeks” OR “update me in 2 weeks” OR “next visit in a month.”

checklist.item: Clear escalation path if adverse events occur
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor explains specifically what to do or who to contact if a defined adverse event occurs — must include both a SYMPTOM trigger AND an ACTION. Match both by synonym, not exact keyword. SYMPTOM triggers include 'severe abdominal pain', 'persistent vomiting', severe hypoglycemia signs, severe allergic reaction, etc. ACTIONs include 'go to hospital', 'seek immediate medical care', 'go to the ER', 'stop the drug and call us', etc. (e.g., 'severe abdominal pain → stop drug, go to ER').
checklist.no_rule: NO if guidance is generic (e.g., 'contact nearby hospital' with no symptom trigger), OR symptom and action are not paired.

examples.yes: “If you feel dizzy or blurred vision, eat chocolate or biscuit immediately.” OR “Severe abdominal pain or persistent vomiting → stop the drug and seek immediate medical care / go to hospital.”

checklist.item: What metrics to track: weight, waist, energy, mood
checklist.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor names at least 2 metrics for the patient to self-track — weight, waist circumference, energy level, mood, blood sugar, blood pressure, etc.
checklist.no_rule: NO if fewer than 2 named.

examples.yes: “Track weight weekly and waist monthly.”
examples.no: “Keep an eye on your weight.” (1 metric).

bonus_counseling_quality.purpose: 8 counseling-quality items from the original chat-message guiding principles. NOT scored — they do NOT change the /100 composite. They are tracked in the Excel for visibility and coaching only. Same YES rule format as the rubric items. Tier weight is set to 0 to make non-scoring explicit.

items.name: Drug choice rationale (semaglutide vs tirzepatide vs liraglutide)
items.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor explicitly compares at least 2 GLP-1 molecules (semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide) AND explains the reason for choosing the prescribed molecule for THIS patient.
items.no_rule: NO if no comparison, or only one molecule named.

items.name: Storage & injection technique
items.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor covers at least 2 of: refrigeration / storage temperature, pen technique, rotation of injection sites.

items.name: Fatty liver / NASH
items.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor asks about fatty liver / NASH, OR LFT status, OR explicitly discusses GLP-1 benefit for liver disease.
items.no_rule: NO if not asked or discussed.

items.name: Cost & adherence plan
items.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor discusses monthly cost, affordability, OR long-term sustainability of GLP-1 therapy in financial terms.
items.no_rule: NO if not discussed even when patient raises cost.

items.name: Injection anxiety / needle phobia
items.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor asks about needle phobia or injection anxiety, OR addresses it proactively (e.g., 'first shot in clinic if you're nervous').

items.name: Realistic weight-loss expectations
items.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor states a SPECIFIC weight-loss percentage range (e.g., 5–15%) AND a time horizon (months).
items.no_rule: NO if no range AND/OR no time horizon.

items.name: Plateau guidance
items.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor pre-warns the patient about weight plateaus (typical at months 4–6 or 8–12) AND offers strategy.

items.name: Patient goals — what does success look like
items.yes_rule: YES iff the doctor asks an open-ended question about what success looks like to the patient (qualitative, not just kilos).
items.no_rule: NO if not asked, OR only weight number is asked.

doctor_name_extraction.purpose: Doctor name is parsed from the source filename, NOT from the transcript prose, because Deepgram regularly mis-transcribes proper nouns (especially Indian names).
doctor_name_extraction.rule: Strip the 'Copy of ' prefix and the '.mpeg' suffix. Strip any trailing dots. The remainder is the canonical doctor name.

call_timestamp.purpose: Unique identifier per call. Combined with Doctor name, uniquely identifies a row when one doctor has multiple calls.
